item.title: W.E.B Du Bois event on February 23 moving to Zoom
item.description: The event has been moved to Zoom due to the snowstorm.

item.title: Berkshire Food Co-op facing financial trouble
item.description: Members of the Co-op’s Board Of Directors and its general manager avoided directly answering questions concerning the Co-op’s finances, including whether it is in danger of closing.

item.title: FILM REVIEW: Fatih Akin’s ‘Amrum’
item.description: It is the last days of World War II, with Berlin about to fall. We see the world through the eyes of a sensitive, thoughtful 12-year-old boy, Nanning, whose mother and father are committed Nazis and who still wears his Hitler Youth uniform.

item.title: STEPHEN COHEN: The Black Magus
item.description: I am always struck by our contradictions—how we interpret, invoke, and discard or simply ignore concepts of morality.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: OLLI presents ‘How We Got to ICE’; Change the Mass Flag at Bushnell-Sage Library; Bidwell House presents Asher Lurie; Berkshire Talking Chronicle presents ‘The 413’; BCC Players auditions; RSYP table talks and community care; Annual Becket Democratic Caucus
item.description: The discussion will explore recent shocking events, particularly those which unfolded in Minnesota.

item.title: Submitted citizens’ petitions for Great Barrington Town Meeting deal with proposed residential tax exemption, ambulance investments
item.description: Resident William Cooke submitted two petitions related to a proposed residential tax exemption, while a third petition by the president of the Southern Berkshire Ambulance Board of Directors seeks $490,000 for two new ambulances.

item.title: ‘Borscht for Ukraine’ fundraiser, Sunday, March 1, at Dewey Hall in Sheffield
item.description: As Ukraine faces its most brutal winter since the war began, a Sheffield family with Ukrainian roots hosts a borscht fundraiser to support Razom for Ukraine's Winter Relief Campaign.

item.title: Infrastructure is the key to equitable housing in the southern Berkshires
item.description: A fair and equitable path forward is the thoughtful expansion of public utilities—town sewer, town water, and publicly available gas or district energy—within and adjacent to our existing village centers.

item.title: BITS & BYTES: Black Violin at The Mahaiwe; Garnell Curtis at American Mural Project; ‘Eno’ at The Crandell; Eryca Nolan at The Foundry; Wanda Houston & the Rejuvenators at Dewey Hall; Heavenly Echoes Gospel Band at Spencertown Academy
item.description: Each powerful performance invites audiences to reflect on their own journeys, discovering that even as we evolve, we're often drawn back to our roots with renewed purpose.

item.title: BRIGHT SPOTS: Week of February 25, 2026
item.description: Standing up for free speech, for funding Minority-Serving Education Institutions, for democracy, workers’ safety, accountability, and justice.
